question: What will the first reported revenues after September 2026 be for the following companies? (Nvidia)

calls.reasoning: Nvidia guided Q3 FY27 revenue to $108.0B +/-2%. In the last five quarters, actual revenue beat the guidance midpoint by 3.8%-5.7% (Q1 FY27 81.6 vs 78; Q2 FY27 96.2 vs 91). Applying that ~4.9% average beat gives ~$113B. Sell-side consensus is ~$108.7B, which typically lags the actual. Tails: a >7.4% beat would push past $116B (possible with China upside, ~6%); missing the guidance range below $105B is very unlikely (~1.5%). The thin Manifold market (4 holders) has a median of ~$112B; its terms match but it is not a reliable anchor.

- Q2 FY27 (reported Aug 26, 2026): revenue $96.2B, +18% q/q, +106% y/y; Data Center $89.0B; guide was $91.0B (+5.7% beat); LSEG consensus was $92.2B.
- Q1 FY27 (May 20, 2026): $81.6B vs $78B guide (+4.6%); consensus $78.8B.

- Upside considerations: Motley Fool (Sept 15, 2026) argues the $108B guide is conservative; any China export resumption is excluded from the guide.
- Searched but not found: any intra-quarter pre-announcement or guidance revision; Kalshi/Polymarket contracts on this figure.

calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the factual core: Q3 FY27 guide of $108.0B ±2%, Q2 FY27 actual $96.2B vs $91B guide, and beats of 3.8-5.7% over recent quarters. Minor factual difference: consensus $108.7B (run 1) vs $109.0B (run 2), which cannot be settled without web access and does not matter since consensus gets no weight. Judgment differences: whether to count the H20-affected Q1 FY26 quarter (+2.6%) — I treat it as a one-off and lean on the 5 clean quarters, but keep a little of the extra downside in the spread; lower escape — one run gave none, but I keep 1.5% because six quarters is too small a sample to call a miss below guidance impossible. Median set at ~$113.0B (the 4.9% mean beat minus a small supply haircut), close to run 1. I carry forward the runs' ~$4.5-4.7B dispersion. Market check: none possible this run (no web access); the runs reported only a thin Manifold market.
